research.job_description_summary: Microsoft hires entry-level software engineers in India. Glassdoor reviews (2024 to 2026) describe a recruiter screen, a coding assessment (a tree problem and a BFS problem in a March 2026 review), a DSA interview that also covers computer science fundamentals (operating systems, databases) and a projects and internships discussion, and an online interview with introductions, behavioral questions and a LeetCode-style problem (April 2026). The official careers pages were not fetched.
limitations: Microsoft's official careers pages were not fetched, so no round is marked DOCUMENTED.

All candidate-reported material comes from a handful of Glassdoor reviews; most give the topic but no problem text, so reported items are original problems on a reported topic and carry one report each.
A review of a November 2024 interview (posted December 2025) supplies the monotonic-stack topic; it is older than the 2025 cutoff for confidence and is marked low confidence.
Round structure differs between reviews (some mention a hiring manager or 'as appropriate' round); the four rounds here are a proposed consolidation.
The reviewer pool includes SDE candidates of unspecified level, so some topics may belong to experienced-hire loops.
Behavioral and system design prompts are original practice and not reported questions.

Evidence handling: practice questions cite no sources; where a source only supplied topic context it is named in the question notes. Practice and job-description-inferred questions are UNVERIFIED and capped at LOW confidence on import.

Review status: answers, samples and cited counts come from the researcher and were not independently re-run; spot checks only. Source titles and some dates are blank because the sources did not show them.
Source pages on LeetCode Discuss and Glassdoor returned HTTP 403 to the CodeArena audit tool (2026-10-11), so the cited questions were not re-confirmed against those pages.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between a process and a thread? What does a context switch involve?
questions.relevance_to_role: Glassdoor reviews describe a DSA round that also covers computer science fundamentals such as operating systems and databases.
questions.expected_answer: A process has its own address space; threads share it. A context switch saves and restores registers, program counter and memory mappings, so it costs more for processes.
follow_ups: Why is thread creation cheaper?
questions.notes: The topic is reported in candidate accounts or guides; this item is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.co.in/Interview/Microsoft-Interview-E1651-RVW101741554.htm.

questions.prompt: What is a deadlock? How can it be prevented or avoided?
questions.relevance_to_role: Glassdoor reviews describe a DSA round that also covers computer science fundamentals such as operating systems and databases.
questions.expected_answer: Four conditions: mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, circular wait. Prevent by breaking one (e.g. lock ordering); avoid with the banker's algorithm; detect and recover.
follow_ups: How does lock ordering work?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial source that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.co.in/Interview/Microsoft-Interview-E1651-RVW101741554.htm.

questions.prompt: Explain virtual memory, paging and what happens on a page fault.
questions.relevance_to_role: Glassdoor reviews describe a DSA round that also covers computer science fundamentals such as operating systems and databases.
questions.expected_answer: Virtual memory maps process addresses to physical frames via page tables. On a page fault the OS loads the missing page from disk, updates the table and restarts the instruction; replacement policies such as LRU choose a victim.
follow_ups: What is thrashing?
questions.notes: Topic comes from an editorial source that does not attribute the question to a candidate; the item itself is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.co.in/Interview/Microsoft-Interview-E1651-RVW101741554.htm.

questions.prompt: What is an index and how does it speed up a query? Compare inner and left joins.
questions.relevance_to_role: Glassdoor reviews describe a DSA round that also covers computer science fundamentals such as operating systems and databases.
questions.expected_answer: An index (often a B-tree) avoids a full scan at the cost of writes and space. Inner join returns matches; left join keeps all left rows with NULLs for non-matches.
follow_ups: When does an index not help?
questions.notes: The topic is reported in candidate accounts or guides; this item is an original practice question. Topic context only (no candidate attribution): https://www.glassdoor.co.in/Interview/Microsoft-Interview-E1651-RVW101741554.htm.

questions.prompt: Explain ACID and two isolation problems such as dirty reads and phantom reads.
questions.relevance_to_role: Glassdoor reviews describe a DSA round that also covers computer science fundamentals such as operating systems and databases.
questions.expected_answer: Atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability. Dirty read: reading uncommitted data; phantom read: new rows appearing in a repeated range query. Isolation levels trade performance for protection.
follow_ups: Which level prevents phantoms?
